sections.skill: Keep a simple categorized ledger and running balance

questions.prompt: What is a ledger?

choices.text: A bank's yearly report on interest rates
A list of every transaction with columns
A promotional flyer that lists product prices
A legal agreement among the owners of an LLC

questions.correct_answer: A list of every transaction with columns
questions.intro: A LEDGER is a list of every transaction with columns such as date, description, category, money in and money out. CATEGORIES group similar items: sales, supplies, shipping, rent, advertising, software, owner draws. Consistent categories let you total each type and spot trends, such as shipping costs rising. A spreadsheet or simple bookkeeping software works. Example running balance: start 500, sale +200 = 700, supplies -80 = 620.

questions.prompt: Start 200, then +50. What is the balance?
questions.intro: A running balance adds money in and subtracts money out, one line at a time. Start with the opening amount. For each line: if money comes in, add; if money goes out, subtract. Example: start 300; +150 = 450; -60 = 390; -40 = 350. Check: opening + total in - total out = 300 + 150 - 100 = 350. Both ways should agree.
